title: Opening and closing file streams
goal: Open a log inside the project, distinguish an absent file from an empty one, and close only a successfully opened stream.

prerequisites.text: Recall checking for NULL from the ownership lesson. The resource here is an open file.
Recall that stdout shows program messages and stdin carries standard input. Project files form a separate source of data.

terms.title: File stream
terms.definition: A connection to an open file. The standard library represents it through FILE * from stdio.h.

terms.title: Relative path
terms.definition: A name within the file area for this run. In input/reading.txt the folder input is part of the name the program looks up.

terms.title: rb mode
terms.definition: Open an existing file for reading without text-mode translation. Opening it successfully says nothing about its content.

sections.title: First check that the log is available
paragraphs: A sensor leaves a reading in input/reading.txt. Before processing, check whether the program can open that exact log. An empty log still exists. A missing log is a separate case.

A Nexus exercise run uses a copy of its project files. Call fopen with a relative path and mode rb. It returns a FILE * on success and NULL on failure. There are several possible reasons to fail. Our message reports the failure itself.
Close each opened stream using fclose. Check its result: 0 means success, EOF means a close error. After attempting to close it, do not use the old FILE * or close it again.
This step checks availability. A populated and an empty log can both produce opened. Distinguishing their contents requires a read operation.

sections.title: Open the sensor log
paragraphs: The run files contain input/reading.txt with 42 and a line feed. The stdin field is empty. Predict whether empty stdin changes what fopen returns.

When you run the program, check the path and the open status first. Then check what happens when the open stream is closed. You can change an empty stdin and an empty file independently. For your own run, use the shift data in the practice file list.
steps: Pass the exact path input/reading.txt and mode rb to fopen.
If fopen returns NULL, print open-error and return before fclose.
After opening succeeds, close the stream. Print opened only if fclose returns 0.

sections.title: Distinguish a build error from an open failure
paragraphs: If Clang reports too few arguments for fopen, check for two arguments: path and mode. That fragment does not run.
If the build succeeds but the program prints open-error, inspect the project file list. A root file named reading.txt differs from input/reading.txt. Pasting 42 into stdin does not create a file.

sections.title: Reproduce a failure with a fixture path
paragraphs: In a separate copy of the example, change only the path to input/absent.txt, which is absent from the file list, and predict the output. Then restore the original path and run with an empty input/reading.txt. Compare the exit codes and explain the difference.

reading.author: ISO/IEC JTC1/SC22/WG14
reading.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 — Programming languages — C
reading.purpose: Check the open mode, fopen return value, and stream-close contract.

selfcheck.prompt: The project contains an empty input/reading.txt. What does the example print if close succeeds?
feedback: The program checks whether an existing file opens. It has not read the contents.
An existing empty file can open successfully.
An empty file does not imply a close error.

selfcheck.prompt: input/reading.txt is absent, but 42 was entered in stdin. What does the program print?
feedback: stdin does not create a file at the requested path.
fopen did not find the file. The fclose call is skipped.
The program does not read stdin.

selfcheck.prompt: After moving the file to the root, a learner gets open-error. What do you check first, and why must this branch skip fclose?
selfcheck.feedback: Compare the project path with the actual filename. fopen returned NULL, so there is no open stream to pass to fclose.

practice.title: Check the shift log
practice.task: A crew keeps the shift start and temperature in the fixture input/shift.txt. Leave stdin empty. Replace NULL near TODO with a call to fopen using the exact path and mode rb. Successful open and close yield opened and exit code 0. An open failure yields open-error and exit code 1 without calling fclose. A close error yields close-error and exit code 1. Leave the file contents untouched.

cases.label: Same filename in a different folder

criteria: An existing log and an existing empty log yield opened. A missing log yields open-error. A line in stdin does not stand in for the file.
Close the stream once after a successful open. Input stays unchanged and no new file is produced.
practice.hint: Find the shift log in the file list. Compare its full relative path with the path in the worked example. Keep the same read mode.

steps.action: Open input/shift.txt in the file list. Return to main.c and run the starter.
steps.why: The file exists. The starter still leaves the pointer set to NULL.

steps.action: Replace NULL on the TODO line and run again.
steps.why: The exact name includes the input folder, and rb opens for reading.

exercises.title: Test a missing file without deleting the log
exercises.task: In a separate copy, temporarily request the absent input/next-shift.txt. Run with empty stdin. Restore the original path. Leave input/shift.txt present but empty in this copy, and run again.
criteria: The first run yields open-error and exit code 1. The second yields opened and exit code 0. Explain why an empty file differs from a missing file.

teaching.scene: At shift change, decide whether a sensor log is available for processing. Test three states separately: a file with a reading, an empty file, and no file at the requested path.

predict.prompt: The example has 42 followed by a newline in input/reading.txt and empty stdin. What line will an ordinary run print? Will the program see the number 42?
predict.answer: fopen opens the requested stream, and fclose returns 0 on a successful close. The program prints opened and exits 0. No operation reads the stream, so 42 stays in the file.

apply.prompt: Keep an empty input/reading.txt and add a root-level reading.txt containing 99 to the same training copy. Predict the status. Now remove only input/reading.txt from that copy. Is the remaining file enough for success?
apply.answer: The first run gives opened if closing succeeds. The program opens the empty file at the exact path. The second run gives open-error and exit code 1. The file at the root cannot stand in for the file in the input folder.

practice.strategy: Locate input/shift.txt in the project. Mark when the open succeeds and what the program reaches in each branch. Compare a populated, an empty, and a missing log.
practice.diagnosis: If both the empty and populated files yield open-error, compare the source path with the file list. If the program attempts a close after open-error, trace how it exits the NULL branch.

syntax.form:
FILE *stream = fopen(path, mode);
if (stream == NULL) { /* handle failure */ }
syntax.explanation: A FILE * represents a stream. Take the error path after a failed open. Close each stream acquired successfully and check the result.
syntax.mistake: Passing NULL to fclose is invalid. Reading an empty file might immediately give EOF even though opening and closing it succeeds.
